classification_signals: Page 1: 'In this expanded second edition of Cognitive Architecture, the authors review new findings in psychology and neuroscience to help architects and planners better understand their clients as the sophisticated mammals they are, arriving in the world with built-in responses to the environment.'
Page 1: 'Cognitive Architecture takes an inside-out approach to design, arguing that the more we understand human behavior, the better we can design and plan for it.'

Page 7: Table of Contents lists chapters like 'A New Foundation: Darwin, Biology, and Cognitive Science', 'Edges Matter: Thigmotaxis (the 'Wall-hugging' Trait)', 'Patterns Matter: Faces and Spaces', 'Shapes Carry Weight: Bilateral Symmetry, (Hierarchy), Curves, and Complexity', 'Storytelling Is Key: We're Wired for Narrative', 'Nature Is Our Context: Biophilia and Biophilic Design', 'Buildings, Biology + Biometrics: Collecting Empirical Data for Evidence-Based Design', and 'The Twenty-First-Century Paradigm Shift in Biology and Psychology Reframes Architecture + Its History'.
Page 33: 'We use Cognitive Architecture to explore how research in psychology and the cognitive sciences can inform our understanding of the impact of buildings and city design on people.'
title: Cognitive Architecture: Designing for How We Respond to the Built Environment
authors: Ann Sussman and Justin B. Hollander, 2021

findings.antecedent: Understanding human beings as artifacts of Darwin's theory of evolution
findings.consequent: Creativity and success in design and planning for them
findings.quote: the more we understand how human beings are an artifact of Darwin's theory of evolution, the more creatively and successfully we will be able to design and plan for them.

findings.consequent: Biological root of the sense of aesthetics
findings.quote: Our sense of aesthetics is at root biological, evolving over millennia.

findings.antecedent: External world aspects important for survival
findings.consequent: Design of human perceptual systems to register these aspects
findings.quote: Our perceptual systems are designed to register aspects of the external world that were important to our survival...

findings.antecedent: Open spaces (center) vs. sides of streets
findings.consequent: Human movement behavior (avoiding center, sticking to sides) due to thigmotaxis as a survival/orientation strategy
findings.quote: people avoid the center of open spaces and tend to stick to the sides of streets, even in car-free zones.

findings.consequent: Human brain's essential orientation toward vision and allocation of more gray matter to visual processing
findings.quote: the human brain is essentially oriented toward vision. More of our gray matter is devoted to creating our visual representation of the world than anything else.

findings.consequent: Brain's prioritization of face processing for evolutionary survival (friend/foe identification)
findings.quote: our mental apparatus does not handle visual inputs equally either-it prioritizes the face. The evolutionary reasons for this are clear: identifying faces quickly, whether friend or foe, proved critical for survival.

findings.consequent: Emotional attachments and memories of places due to unconscious face perception (pareidolia)
findings.quote: Research suggests we also see faces in many of our favorite houses and streetscapes and in so doing most easily and surreptitiously make emotional attachments and memories of these places.

findings.antecedent: Bilateral symmetry in faces and geometric patterns
findings.consequent: Human preference for symmetry and association with power/robustness, reflecting natural selection
findings.quote: human subjects of both sexes were asked to choose between symmetric and asymmetric faces—and even symmetric and asymmetric geometric patterns-they consistently preferred the more symmetrical.

findings.consequent: Unique human wiring for narrative, making storytelling adaptive and leading to art, literature, and identity
findings.quote: Our innate ability to invent stories and create multiple scenarios... is considered highly adaptive.

findings.antecedent: Settings that engage storytelling behavior (e.g., embedded narrative, formal sequences)
findings.quote: people love settings that engage their storytelling behavior.

findings.consequent: Human innate bond with nature (biophilia) and preference for landscapes recalling species-specific past
findings.quote: People also like looking at nature and seeing landscapes that recall their species-specific past.

findings.consequent: Understanding of hidden evolutionary traits and unconscious architectural responses, informing evidence-based design
findings.quote: biometric tools that allow us to see our hidden evolutionary traits at work. Focusing on eye tracking... enables us to tease apart how the architectural experience begins in milliseconds and why it remains mostly outside of our conscious control.

findings.antecedent: Knowledge of human function and evolution's preset responses to stimuli
findings.quote: greater knowledge of how people function, and how evolution has largely preset our responses to external stimuli, has remarkable significance for architectural history and reframes the narrative of how modern architecture, post-WWI, came to be.

It highlights the historical lack of understanding in architecture and planning regarding human biological responses, noting that these unconscious traits were not well-documented or easily observable prior to recent scientific advancements.
minimum_safe_summary: This book, "Cognitive Architecture," proposes a new foundation for architectural and urban design rooted in Darwinian evolution, cognitive science, neuroscience, and psychology. It argues that understanding humans as evolved mammals with built-in responses to the environment is crucial for effective design. Key findings include the unconscious human tendency for thigmotaxis (wall-hugging), the brain's prioritization of visual information and faces for survival, an innate preference for bilateral symmetry, and a unique human wiring for narrative that influences preferences for engaging settings. The book also introduces biometric tools like eye-tracking to reveal these hidden, unconscious responses and suggests that this biological understanding can reframe the history of modern architecture. The provided text does not explicitly state limitations of the book's own approach.

paper_metadata.title: Iconic Mathematics: Math Designed to Suit the Mind
paper_metadata.crossref_title: Iconic Mathematics: Math Designed to Suit the Mind
paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: Mathematics is a struggle for many. To make it more accessible, behavioral and educational scientists are redesigning how it is taught. To a similar end, a few rogue mathematicians and computer scientists are doing something more radical: they are redesigning mathematics itself, improving its ergonomic features. Charles Peirce, an important contributor to ordinary symbolic logic, also introduced a rigorous but non-symbolic, graphical alternative to it that is easier to picture. In the spirit of this iconic logic, George Spencer-Brown founded iconic mathematics. Performing iconic arithmetic, algebra, and even trigonometry, resembles doing calculations on an abacus, which is still popular in education today, has aided humanity for millennia, helps even when it is merely imagined, and ameliorates severe disability in basic computation. Interestingly, whereas some intellectually disabled individuals excel in very complex numerical tasks, others of normal intelligence fail even in very simple ones. A comparison of their wider psychological profiles suggests that iconic mathematics ought to suit the very people traditional mathematics leaves behind.
